Full Data - Pinellas County Model Capstone

Housing Prices, Property Characteristics, and Spatial Dependence

Author

Hunter Evans

Published

November 9, 2026

Project overview

This project models Pinellas County housing prices using a full complete-case analytic dataset.

Three modeling tiers are estimated:

  1. OLS Hedonic Baseline
  2. Bayesian Hierarchical Municipality Model using INLA
  3. Bayesian Spatial SPDE Model using INLA

The primary spatial model uses an INLA Matern SPDE spatial field rather than constructing a CAR adjacency matrix across every individual property coordinate. This preserves the full property-level dataset while keeping the latent spatial model sparse and computationally tractable.

  "tidyverse",

  "sf",
  "sp",
  "INLA",
  "ggplot2",
  "scales",
  "patchwork",
  "broom",
  "knitr",

)

# Install packages from CRAN
cran_packages <- setdiff(
  required_packages,
  rownames(installed.packages())
)

cran_packages <- setdiff(cran_packages, "INLA")

if (length(cran_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(
    cran_packages,
    dependencies = TRUE
  )
}

# ---- 0.2 Install INLA if missing ----
# This uses the Windows binary repository for R 4.5.

if (!requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {

  install.packages(
    "INLA",
    repos = c(
      getOption("repos"),
      INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"
    ),
    dependencies = TRUE
  )
}

1. Clean data and construct predictors

Show code 
# 1. CLEANING AND VARIABLE CONSTRUCTION


df_clean <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(
    sale_year =
      parse_number(sale_year),

    sale_year_c =
      sale_year - 2000,

    adj_price =
      parse_number(adj_price),

    heated_area =
      parse_number(heated_area),

    acreage =
      parse_number(acreage),

    cccl_distance =
      parse_number(cccl_distance),

    tb_distance =
      parse_number(tb_distance),

    icw_distance =
      parse_number(icw_distance),

    x_coord =
      parse_number(x_coord),

    y_coord =
      parse_number(y_coord),
    frontage_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(frontage)
      ),

    seawall_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(seawall)
      ),

    quality_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(quality)
      ),

    foundation_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(foundation)
      ),

    site_city =
      str_squish(site_city),
    frontage_group = case_when(

      is.na(frontage_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      frontage_raw %in% c(
        "NONE",
        "NO",
        "NO FRONTAGE",
        "NO FRONT"
      ) ~
        "None",

      str_detect(
        frontage_raw,
        "BAY|TAMPA BAY"
      ) ~
        "Bay",

      str_detect(
        frontage_raw,
        "LAKE|POND"
      ) ~
        "Lake",

      TRUE ~
        "Other"
    ),
    seawall_group = case_when(

      is.na(seawall_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        seawall_raw,
        "NO SEAWALL|^NO|N|FALSE|^0|NONE"
      ) ~
        "No",

      str_detect(
        seawall_raw,
        "^YES|Y|TRUE|^1$|HAS SEAWALL|SEAWALL"
      ) ~
        "Yes",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    quality_group = case_when(

      is.na(quality_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "ABOVE\\s*AVERAGE|SUPERIOR|EXCELLENT"
      ) ~
        "Above Average",

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "MINIMAL|FAIR"
      ) ~
        "Fair",

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "AVERAGE"
      ) ~
        "Average",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    foundation_group = case_when(

      is.na(foundation_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        foundation_raw,
        "CONTINUOUS"
      ) ~
        "Yes",

      TRUE ~
        "No"
    ),
    stories_num =
      parse_number(stories),

    stories_group = case_when(

      is.na(stories_num) ~
        NA_character_,

      stories_num == 1 ~
        "1",

      stories_num == 2 ~
        "2",

      stories_num >= 3 ~
        "3+",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    barrier_municipality = if_else(

      str_to_upper(site_city) %in% c(
        "ST PETE BEACH",
        "TREASURE ISLAND",
        "MADEIRA BEACH",
        "INDIAN ROCKS BEACH",
        "REDINGTON SHORES",
        "BELLEAIR BEACH",
        "REDINGTON BEACH",
        "NORTH REDINGTON BEACH",
        "INDIAN SHORES",
        "CLEARWATER BEACH"
      ),

      "Barrier",

      "Non-Barrier",

      missing = NA_character_
    ),
    log_price = if_else(
      !is.na(adj_price) &
        adj_price > 0,
      log(adj_price),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(

    sale_year >= 2000,

    sale_year <= 2015,

    !is.na(log_price),

    heated_area > 200,

    !is.na(x_coord),

    !is.na(y_coord),

    !is.na(site_city)
  )


# Variables required for complete-case modeling


model_vars <- c(
  "log_price",
  "sale_year_c",
  "frontage_group",
  "seawall_group",
  "cccl_distance",
  "tb_distance",
  "quality_group",
  "heated_area",
  "acreage",
  "site_city",
  "barrier_municipality",
  "stories_group",
  "foundation_group",
  "x_coord",
  "y_coord"
)


# Complete-case analytic dataset


model_data <- df_clean %>%

  filter(
    if_all(
      all_of(model_vars),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    frontage_group =
      factor(
        frontage_group,
        levels = c(
          "None",
          "Lake",
          "Bay",
          "Other"
        )
      ),

    seawall_group =
      factor(
        seawall_group,
        levels = c(
          "No",
          "Yes"
        )
      ),

    quality_group =
      factor(
        quality_group,
        levels = c(
          "Average",
          "Fair",
          "Above Average"
        )
      ),

    foundation_group =
      factor(
        foundation_group,
        levels = c(
          "No",
          "Yes"
        )
      ),

    stories_group =
      factor(
        stories_group,
        levels = c(
          "1",
          "2",
          "3+"
        )
      ),

    barrier_municipality =
      factor(
        barrier_municipality,
        levels = c(
          "Non-Barrier",
          "Barrier"
        )
      ),

    site_city =
      factor(site_city)
  ) %>%

  droplevels() %>%

  mutate(

    frontage_group =
      relevel(
        frontage_group,
        ref = "None"
      ),

    seawall_group =
      relevel(
        seawall_group,
        ref = "No"
      ),

    quality_group =
      relevel(
        quality_group,
        ref = "Average"
      ),

    foundation_group =
      relevel(
        foundation_group,
        ref = "No"
      ),

    stories_group =
      relevel(
        stories_group,
        ref = "1"
      ),

    barrier_municipality =
      relevel(
        barrier_municipality,
        ref = "Non-Barrier"
      )
  )

rownames(model_data) <- NULL

cleaning_summary <- tibble(
  Stage = c(
    "After initial filters",
    "Final complete-case dataset"
  ),
  Observations = c(
    nrow(df_clean),
    nrow(model_data)
  ),
  Municipalities = c(
    NA_integer_,
    nlevels(model_data$site_city)
  )
)

  cleaning_summary,
  caption = "Data Cleaning and Sample Selection"

bayes_data <- model_data %>%

        scale(cccl_distance)
      ),

      as.numeric(
        scale(tb_distance)
      ),

    heated_area_b =

        scale(heated_area)
      ),

    acreage_b =
      as.numeric(
        scale(acreage)
      )

4.1 Distribution of log adjusted price

7. Prepare projected spatial coordinates

Coordinates are projected UTM Zone 17N coordinates measured in meters. We are unsure whether the original datum is WGS 84 (EPSG:32617) or NAD83 (EPSG:26917).

Show code 
# 7. PREPARE PROJECTED SPATIAL COORDINATES
# Retain the supplied projected coordinates.
# Coordinates are consistent with UTM Zone 17N in meters.

projected_coords <-
  as.matrix(
    bayes_data[
      ,
      c("x_coord", "y_coord")
    ]
  )

colnames(projected_coords) <-
  c("x", "y")

# Verify coordinates.

stopifnot(
  nrow(projected_coords) == nrow(bayes_data),
  ncol(projected_coords) == 2,
  all(is.finite(projected_coords))
)


# Compare possible coordinate reference systems.


test_crs <- function(epsg_code, crs_name) {

  points <- st_as_sf(
    bayes_data,
    coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
    crs = epsg_code
  )

  points_lonlat <- st_transform(
    points,
    4326
  )

  coords <- st_coordinates(points_lonlat)

  tibble(
    coordinate_system = crs_name,
    minimum_longitude = min(coords[, 1]),
    maximum_longitude = max(coords[, 1]),
    minimum_latitude = min(coords[, 2]),
    maximum_latitude = max(coords[, 2])
  )
}

crs_comparison <- bind_rows(

  test_crs(
    32617,
    "WGS 84 / UTM Zone 17N"
  ),

  test_crs(
    26917,
    "NAD83 / UTM Zone 17N"
  ),

  test_crs(
    2882,
    "NAD83(HARN) StatePlane Florida West (feet)"
  )

)


# Compare WGS 84 and NAD83 geographic locations.


coords_32617 <- st_coordinates(
  st_transform(
    st_as_sf(
      bayes_data,
      coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
      crs = 32617
    ),
    4326
  )
)

coords_26917 <- st_coordinates(
  st_transform(
    st_as_sf(
      bayes_data,
      coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
      crs = 26917
    ),
    4326
  )
)

longitude_difference <- max(

)

# Combine results into one readable table.

coordinate_summary <-
  bind_rows(

    tibble(
      coordinate_system = "Original supplied coordinates",
      measurement = c(

      ),

      units = c(

8. Construct computationally efficient INLA SPDE mesh

Show code 
# 8. INLA SPDE MESH

set.seed(12345)

# Mesh construction uses a subset of coordinates.
# This does NOT sample the observations used in the model.
# All complete-case properties remain in the likelihood.
# The sample is only used to construct the mesh efficiently.

mesh_n <- min(15000L, nrow(projected_coords))

mesh_sample_id <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(projected_coords)),
  size = mesh_n
)

mesh_coords <- projected_coords[mesh_sample_id, , drop = FALSE]
Show code 
# BUILD TRIANGULAR SPDE MESH

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  loc = mesh_coords,
  # Minimum distance between mesh points (meters)
  cutoff = 150,
  # Triangle edge lengths (meters)
  # Smaller values produce a more detailed mesh
  # Larger values produce fewer latent spatial nodes
  max.edge = c(1000, 3000),
  # Buffer around observation region (meters)
  offset = c(1000, 3000)
)

9. Define Matern SPDE model

Show code 
# 9. MATERN SPDE

spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  # Matern smoothness: alpha = 2 is the common Matern SPDE construction.
  alpha = 2,
  # PC prior: P(range < 1000 m) = 0.5
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.5),
  # PC prior: P(sigma > 1) = 0.5
  prior.sigma = c(1, 0.5),
  constr = TRUE
)

spde_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = "SPDE latent nodes",
  Value = spde$n.spde
)

Show code

# Fixed effects
fixed_effects <- data.frame(
  intercept = 1,
  sale_year_c = bayes_data$sale_year_c,
  frontage_group = bayes_data$frontage_group,
  seawall_group = bayes_data$seawall_group,
  cccl_distance_b = bayes_data$cccl_distance_b,
  tb_distance_b = bayes_data$tb_distance_b,
  quality_group = bayes_data$quality_group,

  acreage_b = bayes_data$acreage_b,
  barrier_municipality = bayes_data$barrier_municipality,
  stories_group = bayes_data$stories_group,
  foundation_group = bayes_data$foundation_group,
  city_id = bayes_data$city_id
)

# Create stack
spatial_stack <- inla.stack(
  tag = "est",
  data = list(y = bayes_data$log_price),
  A = list(1, A_spde),
  effects = list(fixed_effects, spatial_index),
  remove.unused = FALSE
)

stack_data <- inla.stack.data(spatial_stack)

stack_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = "Stack observations",
  Value = length(stack_data$y)
)

spatial_formula <- y ~
  0 +
  intercept +
  sale_year_c +
  frontage_group +
  seawall_group +
  cccl_distance_b +
  tb_distance_b +

  stories_group +
  foundation_group +
  f(city_id, model = "iid") +
  f(spatial_field, model = spde)

inla_spatial <- inla(
  formula = spatial_formula,
  family = "gaussian",
  data = inla.stack.data(spatial_stack),
  control.predictor = list(

  ),

    return.marginals.predictor = TRUE,

  ),

    strategy = "simplified.laplace"
  ),
  verbose = TRUE
)

Bayesian hierarchical spatial regression estimated using the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA)

Mathematical Specification of the Bayesian Spatial Hedonic Model

The primary model estimates the relationship between housing prices and structural, locational, and geographic characteristics while accounting for municipality-level variation and spatial dependence.

The response variable is the natural logarithm of the adjusted sale price:

\[ Y_i = \log(\text{adj\_price}_i) \]

The observation model is:

\[ Y_i \mid \eta_i,\tau_\epsilon \sim \mathcal{N}(\eta_i,\tau_\epsilon^{-1}) \]

The linear predictor is:

\[ \begin{aligned} \eta_i =\;& \beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{SaleYear}_i + \boldsymbol{\beta}_2^\top \text{Frontage}_i + \beta_3 \text{Seawall}_i \\ &+ \beta_4 \text{CCCLDistance}_i + \beta_5 \text{TBDistance}_i + \boldsymbol{\beta}_6^\top \text{Quality}_i \\ &+ \beta_7 \text{HeatedArea}_i + \beta_8 \text{Acreage}_i + \beta_9 \text{BarrierMunicipality}_i \\ &+ \boldsymbol{\beta}_{10}^\top \text{Stories}_i + \boldsymbol{\beta}_{11}^\top \text{Foundation}_i \\ &+ u_{c(i)} + w(\mathbf{s}_i) \end{aligned} \]

where:

  • i indexes individual property sales.
  • 0 is the overall intercept.
  • The coefficients represent fixed effects associated with housing characteristics and location.
  • Categorical predictors are represented by indicator variables relative to their reference categories.
  • uc(i) is the municipality-specific random intercept for the municipality containing property i.
  • w(si) is the spatially structured random effect at the property’s geographic coordinates.
  • is the observation-level error precision.

The municipality-level random effects are modeled as:

\[ u_j \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim} \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2_{\text{city}}) \]

The spatial random effect is modeled as a Matérn Gaussian random field:

\[ w(\mathbf{s}) \sim \text{Matérn}(\sigma^2_{\text{spatial}},\rho,\nu) \]

The Matérn spatial field is represented computationally using the Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) approach:

\[ (\kappa^2-\Delta)^{\alpha/2} \left(\tau_{\text{SPDE}}w(\mathbf{s})\right) = \mathcal{W}(\mathbf{s}) \]

where is the Laplacian operator, W(s) is Gaussian white noise, controls the spatial range, and SPDE is a scaling parameter. For this model, the SPDE uses:

\[ \alpha=2,\qquad d=2,\qquad \nu=\alpha-\frac{d}{2}=1 \]

The approximate relationship between the Matérn range and is:

\[ \rho=\frac{\sqrt{8\nu}}{\kappa} \]

The SPDE model uses penalized-complexity (PC) priors for the spatial range and marginal standard deviation:

\[ P(\rho < 1000)=0.5 \]

\[ P(\sigma_{\text{spatial}}>1)=0.5 \]

These priors correspond to the INLA specification prior.range = c(1000, 0.5) and prior.sigma = c(1, 0.5), assuming the projected coordinate system uses meters.

The complete model is estimated using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA), which provides approximate Bayesian inference for the fixed effects, municipality-level random effects, spatial field, and model hyperparameters.

spatial_fixed_effects

# FIXED EFFECTS: CLEAN TABLE

spatial_fixed_effects_clean <-
  spatial_fixed_effects %>%

  rownames_to_column(
    var = "Term"
  ) %>%

  select(
    Term,
    mean,
    sd,
    `0.025quant`,
    `0.5quant`,
    `0.975quant`
  )

spatial_fixed_effects_clean

21. INLA prediction accuracy

Show code 
# 21. PREDICTION ACCURACY


inla_rmse <-
  sqrt(
    mean(
      bayes_data$inla_residual^2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

inla_mae <-
  mean(
    abs(
      bayes_data$inla_residual
    ),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

inla_r2 <-
  1 -

  sum(
    bayes_data$inla_residual^2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) /

  sum(
    (
      bayes_data$log_price -
        mean(
          bayes_data$log_price,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    )^2,

    na.rm = TRUE
  )

inla_accuracy <-
  tibble(

    Model =
      "INLA spatial SPDE",

    N =
      nrow(bayes_data),

    RMSE =
      inla_rmse,

    MAE =
      inla_mae,

    R_squared =
      inla_r2
  )

inla_accuracy

# Project overview

This project models Pinellas County housing prices using a full complete-case
analytic dataset.

Three modeling tiers are estimated:

1. OLS Hedonic Baseline
2. Bayesian Hierarchical Municipality Model using INLA
3. Bayesian Spatial SPDE Model using INLA

The primary spatial model uses an INLA Matern SPDE spatial field rather than
constructing a CAR adjacency matrix across every individual property
coordinate. This preserves the full property-level dataset while keeping the
latent spatial model sparse and computationally tractable.

# 0. Packages and data import

```{r}
# SECTION 0: PACKAGES AND DATA IMPORT

required_packages <- c(
  "tidyverse",
  "janitor",
  "lubridate",
  "sf",
  "sp",
  "INLA",
  "ggplot2",
  "scales",
  "patchwork",
  "broom",
  "knitr",
  "viridis",
  "viridisLite"
)

# Install packages from CRAN
cran_packages <- setdiff(
  required_packages,
  rownames(installed.packages())
)

cran_packages <- setdiff(cran_packages, "INLA")

if (length(cran_packages) > 0) {
  install.packages(
    cran_packages,
    dependencies = TRUE
  )
}

# ---- 0.2 Install INLA if missing ----
# This uses the Windows binary repository for R 4.5.

if (!requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {

  install.packages(
    "INLA",
    repos = c(
      getOption("repos"),
      INLA = "https://inla.r-inla-download.org/R/stable"
    ),
    dependencies = TRUE
  )
}

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(lubridate)
library(sf)
library(sp)
library(INLA)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)
library(patchwork)
library(broom)
library(knitr)
library(viridis)
library(viridisLite)


analysis_version <- "pinellas_full_data_capstone_inla_spde_v1"


data_path <- paste0(
  "G:/",
  ".shortcut-targets-by-id/1IwJJwifiMkxN1ZtZ-lx4TooG6WGbO18w/",
  "Alderfer and Evans/1-data/pinellasdata.csv"
)

# Confirm that the file exists before importing
if (!file.exists(data_path)) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "DATA FILE NOT FOUND.\n",
      "Check that the Google Drive location is available.\n",
      "Current path: ",
      data_path
    )
  )
}

required_17_columns <- c(
  "uid",
  "parcelid",
  "sale_year",
  "adj_price",
  "heated_area",
  "acreage",
  "stories",
  "quality",
  "foundation",
  "seawall",
  "cccl_distance",
  "tb_distance",
  "icw_distance",
  "frontage",
  "x_coord",
  "y_coord",
  "site_city"
)

# ---- 0.7 Import the full dataset ----
# Import as character first to avoid accidental type conversion.
# Numeric conversion will happen during the cleaning section.

raw_data <- readr::read_csv(
  file = data_path,
  col_select = tidyselect::all_of(required_17_columns),
  col_types = readr::cols(
    .default = readr::col_character()
  ),
  na = c(
    "",
    "NA",
    "N/A",
    ".",
    "null",
    "NULL",
    "*"
  ),
  progress = TRUE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# ---- 0.8 Verify imported dataset ----

# Import verification

import_summary <- tibble(
  Check = c(
    "File exists",
    "Data object class",
    "Observations imported",
    "Variables imported"
  ),
  Result = c(
    file.exists(data_path),
    paste(class(raw_data), collapse = ", "),
    format(nrow(raw_data), big.mark = ","),
    ncol(raw_data)
  )
)

knitr::kable(import_summary, caption = "Data Import Verification")

# Missing values by column

missing_summary <- tibble(Variable = names(raw_data), Missing = colSums(is.na(raw_data))) %>%
  arrange(desc(Missing))

knitr::kable(missing_summary, caption = "Missing Values by Variable")

# ---- 0.9 Stop if the import does not match expectations ----

if (!is.data.frame(raw_data)) {
  stop("Import failed: raw_data is not a data frame.")
}

if (ncol(raw_data) != 17) {
  stop(
    paste(
      "Expected 17 columns but imported",
      ncol(raw_data)
    )
  )
}

if (!all(required_17_columns %in% names(raw_data))) {
  stop("One or more required columns are missing.")
}

if (nrow(raw_data) == 0) {
  stop("The imported dataset contains zero rows.")
}
```

# 1. Clean data and construct predictors

```{r}
# 1. CLEANING AND VARIABLE CONSTRUCTION


df_clean <- raw_data %>%
  mutate(
    sale_year =
      parse_number(sale_year),

    sale_year_c =
      sale_year - 2000,

    adj_price =
      parse_number(adj_price),

    heated_area =
      parse_number(heated_area),

    acreage =
      parse_number(acreage),

    cccl_distance =
      parse_number(cccl_distance),

    tb_distance =
      parse_number(tb_distance),

    icw_distance =
      parse_number(icw_distance),

    x_coord =
      parse_number(x_coord),

    y_coord =
      parse_number(y_coord),
    frontage_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(frontage)
      ),

    seawall_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(seawall)
      ),

    quality_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(quality)
      ),

    foundation_raw =
      str_squish(
        str_to_upper(foundation)
      ),

    site_city =
      str_squish(site_city),
    frontage_group = case_when(

      is.na(frontage_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      frontage_raw %in% c(
        "NONE",
        "NO",
        "NO FRONTAGE",
        "NO FRONT"
      ) ~
        "None",

      str_detect(
        frontage_raw,
        "BAY|TAMPA BAY"
      ) ~
        "Bay",

      str_detect(
        frontage_raw,
        "LAKE|POND"
      ) ~
        "Lake",

      TRUE ~
        "Other"
    ),
    seawall_group = case_when(

      is.na(seawall_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        seawall_raw,
        "NO SEAWALL|^NO|N|FALSE|^0|NONE"
      ) ~
        "No",

      str_detect(
        seawall_raw,
        "^YES|Y|TRUE|^1$|HAS SEAWALL|SEAWALL"
      ) ~
        "Yes",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    quality_group = case_when(

      is.na(quality_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "ABOVE\\s*AVERAGE|SUPERIOR|EXCELLENT"
      ) ~
        "Above Average",

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "MINIMAL|FAIR"
      ) ~
        "Fair",

      str_detect(
        quality_raw,
        "AVERAGE"
      ) ~
        "Average",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    foundation_group = case_when(

      is.na(foundation_raw) ~
        NA_character_,

      str_detect(
        foundation_raw,
        "CONTINUOUS"
      ) ~
        "Yes",

      TRUE ~
        "No"
    ),
    stories_num =
      parse_number(stories),

    stories_group = case_when(

      is.na(stories_num) ~
        NA_character_,

      stories_num == 1 ~
        "1",

      stories_num == 2 ~
        "2",

      stories_num >= 3 ~
        "3+",

      TRUE ~
        NA_character_
    ),
    barrier_municipality = if_else(

      str_to_upper(site_city) %in% c(
        "ST PETE BEACH",
        "TREASURE ISLAND",
        "MADEIRA BEACH",
        "INDIAN ROCKS BEACH",
        "REDINGTON SHORES",
        "BELLEAIR BEACH",
        "REDINGTON BEACH",
        "NORTH REDINGTON BEACH",
        "INDIAN SHORES",
        "CLEARWATER BEACH"
      ),

      "Barrier",

      "Non-Barrier",

      missing = NA_character_
    ),
    log_price = if_else(
      !is.na(adj_price) &
        adj_price > 0,
      log(adj_price),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(

    sale_year >= 2000,

    sale_year <= 2015,

    !is.na(log_price),

    heated_area > 200,

    !is.na(x_coord),

    !is.na(y_coord),

    !is.na(site_city)
  )


# Variables required for complete-case modeling


model_vars <- c(
  "log_price",
  "sale_year_c",
  "frontage_group",
  "seawall_group",
  "cccl_distance",
  "tb_distance",
  "quality_group",
  "heated_area",
  "acreage",
  "site_city",
  "barrier_municipality",
  "stories_group",
  "foundation_group",
  "x_coord",
  "y_coord"
)


# Complete-case analytic dataset


model_data <- df_clean %>%

  filter(
    if_all(
      all_of(model_vars),
      ~ !is.na(.x)
    )
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    frontage_group =
      factor(
        frontage_group,
        levels = c(
          "None",
          "Lake",
          "Bay",
          "Other"
        )
      ),

    seawall_group =
      factor(
        seawall_group,
        levels = c(
          "No",
          "Yes"
        )
      ),

    quality_group =
      factor(
        quality_group,
        levels = c(
          "Average",
          "Fair",
          "Above Average"
        )
      ),

    foundation_group =
      factor(
        foundation_group,
        levels = c(
          "No",
          "Yes"
        )
      ),

    stories_group =
      factor(
        stories_group,
        levels = c(
          "1",
          "2",
          "3+"
        )
      ),

    barrier_municipality =
      factor(
        barrier_municipality,
        levels = c(
          "Non-Barrier",
          "Barrier"
        )
      ),

    site_city =
      factor(site_city)
  ) %>%

  droplevels() %>%

  mutate(

    frontage_group =
      relevel(
        frontage_group,
        ref = "None"
      ),

    seawall_group =
      relevel(
        seawall_group,
        ref = "No"
      ),

    quality_group =
      relevel(
        quality_group,
        ref = "Average"
      ),

    foundation_group =
      relevel(
        foundation_group,
        ref = "No"
      ),

    stories_group =
      relevel(
        stories_group,
        ref = "1"
      ),

    barrier_municipality =
      relevel(
        barrier_municipality,
        ref = "Non-Barrier"
      )
  )

rownames(model_data) <- NULL

cleaning_summary <- tibble(
  Stage = c(
    "After initial filters",
    "Final complete-case dataset"
  ),
  Observations = c(
    nrow(df_clean),
    nrow(model_data)
  ),
  Municipalities = c(
    NA_integer_,
    nlevels(model_data$site_city)
  )
)

knitr::kable(
  cleaning_summary,
  caption = "Data Cleaning and Sample Selection"
)
```

# 5. Model 1 — OLS hedonic baseline

```{r}
# 5. OLS HEDONIC BASELINE

hedonic_formula <- log_price ~
  sale_year_c +
  frontage_group +
  seawall_group +
  cccl_distance +
  tb_distance +
  quality_group +
  heated_area +
  acreage +
  barrier_municipality +
  stories_group +
  foundation_group

ols_model <- lm(
  formula = hedonic_formula,
  data = model_data
)

summary(ols_model)

ols_fit <- tibble(
  Model = "OLS hedonic baseline",
  N = nobs(ols_model),
  R_squared = summary(ols_model)$r.squared,
  Adjusted_R_squared = summary(ols_model)$adj.r.squared,
  AIC = AIC(ols_model),
  BIC = BIC(ols_model),
  RMSE = sqrt(mean(residuals(ols_model)^2)),
  MAE = mean(abs(residuals(ols_model)))
)

ols_fit
```

# 6. Model 2 — INLA hierarchical municipality model

```{r}
# 6. INLA HIERARCHICAL MUNICIPALITY MODEL

city_formula <- log_price ~
  sale_year_c +
  frontage_group +
  seawall_group +
  cccl_distance_b +
  tb_distance_b +
  quality_group +
  heated_area_b +
  acreage_b +
  barrier_municipality +
  stories_group +
  foundation_group +
  f(city_id, model = "iid")

inla_city <- inla(
  formula = city_formula,
  family = "gaussian",
  data = bayes_data,
  control.predictor = list(
    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1
  ),
  control.compute = list(
    dic = TRUE,
    waic = TRUE,
    cpo = TRUE,
    return.marginals.predictor = TRUE
  ),
  control.inla = list(
    strategy = "simplified.laplace"
  ),
  verbose = FALSE
)

summary(inla_city)
```

# 7. Prepare projected spatial coordinates

Coordinates are projected UTM Zone 17N coordinates measured in meters.  We are unsure whether the original datum is WGS 84 (EPSG:32617) or NAD83 (EPSG:26917).

```{r}
# 7. PREPARE PROJECTED SPATIAL COORDINATES
# Retain the supplied projected coordinates.
# Coordinates are consistent with UTM Zone 17N in meters.

projected_coords <-
  as.matrix(
    bayes_data[
      ,
      c("x_coord", "y_coord")
    ]
  )

colnames(projected_coords) <-
  c("x", "y")

# Verify coordinates.

stopifnot(
  nrow(projected_coords) == nrow(bayes_data),
  ncol(projected_coords) == 2,
  all(is.finite(projected_coords))
)


# Compare possible coordinate reference systems.


test_crs <- function(epsg_code, crs_name) {

  points <- st_as_sf(
    bayes_data,
    coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
    crs = epsg_code
  )

  points_lonlat <- st_transform(
    points,
    4326
  )

  coords <- st_coordinates(points_lonlat)

  tibble(
    coordinate_system = crs_name,
    minimum_longitude = min(coords[, 1]),
    maximum_longitude = max(coords[, 1]),
    minimum_latitude = min(coords[, 2]),
    maximum_latitude = max(coords[, 2])
  )
}

crs_comparison <- bind_rows(

  test_crs(
    32617,
    "WGS 84 / UTM Zone 17N"
  ),

  test_crs(
    26917,
    "NAD83 / UTM Zone 17N"
  ),

  test_crs(
    2882,
    "NAD83(HARN) StatePlane Florida West (feet)"
  )

)


# Compare WGS 84 and NAD83 geographic locations.


coords_32617 <- st_coordinates(
  st_transform(
    st_as_sf(
      bayes_data,
      coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
      crs = 32617
    ),
    4326
  )
)

coords_26917 <- st_coordinates(
  st_transform(
    st_as_sf(
      bayes_data,
      coords = c("x_coord", "y_coord"),
      crs = 26917
    ),
    4326
  )
)

longitude_difference <- max(
  abs(coords_32617[, 1] - coords_26917[, 1])
)

latitude_difference <- max(
  abs(coords_32617[, 2] - coords_26917[, 2])
)


# Combine results into one readable table.

coordinate_summary <-
  bind_rows(

    tibble(
      coordinate_system = "Original supplied coordinates",
      measurement = c(
        "Number of observations",
        "Minimum X",
        "Maximum X",
        "Minimum Y",
        "Maximum Y"
      ),
      value = c(
        nrow(projected_coords),
        min(projected_coords[, 1]),
        max(projected_coords[, 1]),
        min(projected_coords[, 2]),
        max(projected_coords[, 2])
      ),
      units = c(
        "observations",
        "meters",
        "meters",
        "meters",
        "meters"
      )
    ),

    crs_comparison %>%
      pivot_longer(
        cols = -coordinate_system,
        names_to = "measurement",
        values_to = "value"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        measurement = recode(
          measurement,
          minimum_longitude = "Minimum longitude",
          maximum_longitude = "Maximum longitude",
          minimum_latitude = "Minimum latitude",
          maximum_latitude = "Maximum latitude"
        ),
        units = "decimal degrees"
      )

  )

knitr::kable(
  coordinate_summary,
  digits = 6,
  caption = "Spatial Coordinates and Coordinate Reference System Comparison",
  col.names = c(
    "Coordinate system",
    "Measurement",
    "Value",
    "Units"
  )
)

head(bayes_data[, c("x_coord", "y_coord")], 20)
```


# 8. Construct computationally efficient INLA SPDE mesh

```{r}
# 8. INLA SPDE MESH

set.seed(12345)

# Mesh construction uses a subset of coordinates.
# This does NOT sample the observations used in the model.
# All complete-case properties remain in the likelihood.
# The sample is only used to construct the mesh efficiently.

mesh_n <- min(15000L, nrow(projected_coords))

mesh_sample_id <- sample(
  seq_len(nrow(projected_coords)),
  size = mesh_n
)

mesh_coords <- projected_coords[mesh_sample_id, , drop = FALSE]
```

```{r}
# BUILD TRIANGULAR SPDE MESH

mesh <- inla.mesh.2d(
  loc = mesh_coords,
  # Minimum distance between mesh points (meters)
  cutoff = 150,
  # Triangle edge lengths (meters)
  # Smaller values produce a more detailed mesh
  # Larger values produce fewer latent spatial nodes
  max.edge = c(1000, 3000),
  # Buffer around observation region (meters)
  offset = c(1000, 3000)
)

mesh_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = c("Mesh vertices", "Mesh triangles", "Coordinates used for mesh construction"),
  Value = c(nrow(mesh$loc), nrow(mesh$graph$tv), nrow(mesh_coords))
)

knitr::kable(mesh_summary, caption = "SPDE Mesh Diagnostics")
```

## 8.1 Plot mesh

```{r}
# MESH VISUALIZATION

plot(mesh, asp = 1, main = "INLA SPDE Mesh - Pinellas County")
points(mesh_coords, pch = 16, cex = 0.1)
```

# 9. Define Matern SPDE model

```{r}
# 9. MATERN SPDE

spde <- inla.spde2.pcmatern(
  mesh = mesh,
  # Matern smoothness: alpha = 2 is the common Matern SPDE construction.
  alpha = 2,
  # PC prior: P(range < 1000 m) = 0.5
  prior.range = c(1000, 0.5),
  # PC prior: P(sigma > 1) = 0.5
  prior.sigma = c(1, 0.5),
  constr = TRUE
)

spde_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = "SPDE latent nodes",
  Value = spde$n.spde
)

knitr::kable(spde_summary, caption = "SPDE Model Summary")
```

# 10. Create SPDE projection matrix

```{r}
# 10. SPDE PROJECTION MATRIX

A_spde <- inla.spde.make.A(
  mesh = mesh,
  loc = projected_coords
)

projection_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = c("Projection matrix rows", "Projection matrix columns", "SPDE latent nodes"),
  Value = c(nrow(A_spde), ncol(A_spde), spde$n.spde)
)

knitr::kable(
  projection_summary,
  caption = "SPDE Projection Matrix Dimensions"
)
```

# 11. Create INLA spatial index

```{r}
# 11. SPATIAL INDEX

spatial_index <- inla.spde.make.index(name = "spatial_field", n.spde = spde$n.spde)
```

# 12. Create INLA model stack

```{r}
# 12. INLA STACK

# Fixed effects
fixed_effects <- data.frame(
  intercept = 1,
  sale_year_c = bayes_data$sale_year_c,
  frontage_group = bayes_data$frontage_group,
  seawall_group = bayes_data$seawall_group,
  cccl_distance_b = bayes_data$cccl_distance_b,
  tb_distance_b = bayes_data$tb_distance_b,
  quality_group = bayes_data$quality_group,
  heated_area_b = bayes_data$heated_area_b,
  acreage_b = bayes_data$acreage_b,
  barrier_municipality = bayes_data$barrier_municipality,
  stories_group = bayes_data$stories_group,
  foundation_group = bayes_data$foundation_group,
  city_id = bayes_data$city_id
)

# Create stack
spatial_stack <- inla.stack(
  tag = "est",
  data = list(y = bayes_data$log_price),
  A = list(1, A_spde),
  effects = list(fixed_effects, spatial_index),
  remove.unused = FALSE
)

stack_data <- inla.stack.data(spatial_stack)

stack_summary <- tibble(
  Metric = "Stack observations",
  Value = length(stack_data$y)
)

knitr::kable(
  stack_summary,
  caption = "INLA Stack Summary"
)
```

# 13. Primary INLA spatial model

```{r}
# 13. PRIMARY INLA SPATIAL MODEL

spatial_formula <- y ~
  0 +
  intercept +
  sale_year_c +
  frontage_group +
  seawall_group +
  cccl_distance_b +
  tb_distance_b +
  quality_group +
  heated_area_b +
  acreage_b +
  barrier_municipality +
  stories_group +
  foundation_group +
  f(city_id, model = "iid") +
  f(spatial_field, model = spde)

inla_spatial <- inla(
  formula = spatial_formula,
  family = "gaussian",
  data = inla.stack.data(spatial_stack),
  control.predictor = list(
    A = inla.stack.A(spatial_stack),
    compute = TRUE,
    link = 1
  ),
  control.compute = list(
    dic = TRUE,
    waic = TRUE,
    cpo = TRUE,
    return.marginals.predictor = TRUE,
    config = TRUE
  ),
  control.inla = list(
    strategy = "simplified.laplace"
  ),
  verbose = TRUE
)

summary(inla_spatial)
```

Bayesian hierarchical spatial regression estimated using the Integrated Nested Laplace Approximation (INLA)

## Mathematical Specification of the Bayesian Spatial Hedonic Model

The primary model estimates the relationship between housing prices and structural, locational, and geographic characteristics while accounting for municipality-level variation and spatial dependence.

The response variable is the natural logarithm of the adjusted sale price:

$$
Y_i = \log(\text{adj\_price}_i)
$$

The observation model is:

$$
Y_i \mid \eta_i,\tau_\epsilon
\sim
\mathcal{N}(\eta_i,\tau_\epsilon^{-1})
$$

The linear predictor is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\eta_i =\;&
\beta_0
+ \beta_1 \text{SaleYear}_i
+ \boldsymbol{\beta}_2^\top \text{Frontage}_i
+ \beta_3 \text{Seawall}_i \\
&+ \beta_4 \text{CCCLDistance}_i
+ \beta_5 \text{TBDistance}_i
+ \boldsymbol{\beta}_6^\top \text{Quality}_i \\
&+ \beta_7 \text{HeatedArea}_i
+ \beta_8 \text{Acreage}_i
+ \beta_9 \text{BarrierMunicipality}_i \\
&+ \boldsymbol{\beta}_{10}^\top \text{Stories}_i
+ \boldsymbol{\beta}_{11}^\top \text{Foundation}_i \\
&+ u_{c(i)}
+ w(\mathbf{s}_i)
\end{aligned}
$$

where:

- i indexes individual property sales.
- 0 is the overall intercept.
- The  coefficients represent fixed effects associated with housing characteristics and location.
- Categorical predictors are represented by indicator variables relative to their reference categories.
- uc(i) is the municipality-specific random intercept for the municipality containing property i.
- w(si) is the spatially structured random effect at the property's geographic coordinates.
-  is the observation-level error precision.

The municipality-level random effects are modeled as:

$$
u_j \overset{\text{iid}}{\sim}
\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^2_{\text{city}})
$$

The spatial random effect is modeled as a Matérn Gaussian random field:

$$
w(\mathbf{s}) \sim
\text{Matérn}(\sigma^2_{\text{spatial}},\rho,\nu)
$$

The Matérn spatial field is represented computationally using the Stochastic Partial Differential Equation (SPDE) approach:

$$
(\kappa^2-\Delta)^{\alpha/2}
\left(\tau_{\text{SPDE}}w(\mathbf{s})\right)
=
\mathcal{W}(\mathbf{s})
$$

where  is the Laplacian operator, W(s) is Gaussian white noise,  controls the spatial range, and SPDE is a scaling parameter. For this model, the SPDE uses:

$$
\alpha=2,\qquad d=2,\qquad
\nu=\alpha-\frac{d}{2}=1
$$

The approximate relationship between the Matérn range and  is:

$$
\rho=\frac{\sqrt{8\nu}}{\kappa}
$$

The SPDE model uses penalized-complexity (PC) priors for the spatial range and marginal standard deviation:

$$
P(\rho < 1000)=0.5
$$

$$
P(\sigma_{\text{spatial}}>1)=0.5
$$

These priors correspond to the INLA specification `prior.range = c(1000, 0.5)` and `prior.sigma = c(1, 0.5)`, assuming the projected coordinate system uses meters.

The complete model is estimated using Integrated Nested Laplace Approximations (INLA), which provides approximate Bayesian inference for the fixed effects, municipality-level random effects, spatial field, and model hyperparameters.

```{r}
# MODEL OUTPUT: COEFFICIENTS, RANDOM EFFECTS, PRIORS, AND FIT

# 1. Fixed-effect coefficient estimates
fixed_effect_output <- inla_spatial$summary.fixed

print("FIXED EFFECT COEFFICIENTS")
print(fixed_effect_output)

# 2. Municipality random effects
municipality_output <- inla_spatial$summary.random$city_id

print("MUNICIPALITY RANDOM EFFECTS")
print(municipality_output)

# 3. Spatial random field summary
spatial_output <- inla_spatial$summary.random$spatial_field

print("SPATIAL RANDOM FIELD")
print(spatial_output)

# 4. Hyperparameter estimates
hyperparameter_output <- inla_spatial$summary.hyperpar

print("MODEL HYPERPARAMETERS")
print(hyperparameter_output)

# 5. Model fit statistics
model_fit_output <- data.frame(
  DIC = inla_spatial$dic$dic,
  WAIC = inla_spatial$waic$waic,
  log_marginal_likelihood = inla_spatial$mlik[1]
)

print("MODEL FIT STATISTICS")
print(model_fit_output)

# 6. Save all model output tables
write.csv(
  fixed_effect_output,
  "fixed_effect_coefficients.csv"
)

write.csv(
  municipality_output,
  "municipality_random_effects.csv"
)

write.csv(
  spatial_output,
  "spatial_random_effects.csv"
)

write.csv(
  hyperparameter_output,
  "model_hyperparameters.csv"
)

write.csv(
  model_fit_output,
  "model_fit_statistics.csv",
  row.names = FALSE
)
```

# 20. Extract fitted values

```{r}
# 20. FITTED VALUES

# Extract fitted values from INLA
fitted_summary <- inla_spatial$summary.fitted.values

# Identify observed-data rows
estimation_index <- inla.stack.index(spatial_stack, tag = "est")$data

# Extract fitted values for observed observations only
observed_fitted <- fitted_summary$mean[estimation_index]

# Verify dimensions
if (length(observed_fitted) != nrow(bayes_data)) {
  stop(paste0(
    "ERROR: Fitted values do not match bayes_data. ",
    "Fitted values: ", length(observed_fitted),
    "; Observations: ", nrow(bayes_data)
  ))
}

# Assign fitted values
bayes_data$inla_fitted <- observed_fitted

# Calculate residuals
bayes_data$inla_residual <- bayes_data$log_price - bayes_data$inla_fitted

# Summary statistics
fitted_value_summary <- tibble(
  Statistic = c("Total INLA fitted values", "Observed-data stack rows", "Bayesian dataset rows"),
  Value = c(length(fitted_summary$mean), length(estimation_index), nrow(bayes_data))
)

print(fitted_value_summary)

model_value_summary <- tibble(
  Variable = c("Fitted values", "Residuals"),
  Minimum = c(min(bayes_data$inla_fitted), min(bayes_data$inla_residual)),
  Mean = c(mean(bayes_data$inla_fitted), mean(bayes_data$inla_residual)),
  Median = c(median(bayes_data$inla_fitted), median(bayes_data$inla_residual)),
  Maximum = c(max(bayes_data$inla_fitted), max(bayes_data$inla_residual))
)

print(model_value_summary)
```

# 21. INLA prediction accuracy

```{r}
# 21. PREDICTION ACCURACY


inla_rmse <-
  sqrt(
    mean(
      bayes_data$inla_residual^2,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  )

inla_mae <-
  mean(
    abs(
      bayes_data$inla_residual
    ),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

inla_r2 <-
  1 -

  sum(
    bayes_data$inla_residual^2,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) /

  sum(
    (
      bayes_data$log_price -
        mean(
          bayes_data$log_price,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    )^2,

    na.rm = TRUE
  )

inla_accuracy <-
  tibble(

    Model =
      "INLA spatial SPDE",

    N =
      nrow(bayes_data),

    RMSE =
      inla_rmse,

    MAE =
      inla_mae,

    R_squared =
      inla_r2
  )

inla_accuracy
```

```{r}
set.seed(12345)

ggplot(

  aes(
    x = x_coord,
    y = y_coord,
    color = inla_residual

) +

  geom_point(
    alpha = 0.15,
    size = 0.3
  ) +

  scale_color_viridis_c(

  labs(
    title =
      "Spatial Distribution of INLA Residuals",
    subtitle =
      "30,000-observation visualization sample",
    x =
      "X coordinate",
    y =
      "Y coordinate",
    color =
      "Residual"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# The SPDE random effect is defined at mesh vertices.


mesh_field <-
  tibble(

    x =
      mesh$loc[, 1],

    y =
      mesh$loc[, 2],

    spatial_effect =
      spatial_field_summary$mean,

      spatial_field_summary$`0.025quant`,

    spatial_upper =
      spatial_field_summary$`0.975quant`
```

# 28. Municipality effects plot

```{r}
# 28. MUNICIPALITY EFFECT PLOT


# Extract municipality random effects
city_effect_plot <-
  inla_spatial$summary.random$city_id %>%

  # INLA stores municipality IDs in the ID column
  mutate(
    city_id = as.integer(ID)
  ) %>%

  # Join municipality names
  left_join(
    bayes_data %>%
      select(
        city_id,
        site_city
      ) %>%
      distinct(),
    by = "city_id"
  ) %>%

  # Arrange by estimated municipality effect
  arrange(
    mean
  )

print(
  head(city_effect_plot)
)

# Check for unmatched municipality names
if (any(is.na(city_effect_plot$site_city))) {
  warning(
    "Some municipality IDs did not match municipality names."
  )
}

# Plot municipality random effects
ggplot(
  city_effect_plot,
  aes(
    x = reorder(site_city, mean),
    y = mean
  )
) +

  geom_point(
    size = 2,
    color = "steelblue"
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = `0.025quant`,
      ymax = `0.975quant`
    ),
    width = 0.2
  ) +

  coord_flip() +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "red"
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Municipality Random Effects",
    subtitle = "INLA Spatial Model",
    x = "Municipality",
    y = "Estimated Random Effect (Log Price)"
  ) +

  theme_minimal()

```
